extracted.intended_audience: presidents of invited universities; early-career faculty nominees and their referees (potential applicants and institutional nominators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for nomination, application, selection, and reporting for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation’s Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering (2025). Covers eligibility, required materials, letter requirements, review process, award terms, and reporting expectations for invited institutions and nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — career stage and PI eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be faculty members who are eligible to serve as principal investigators engaged in research in the natural and physical sciences or engineering and must be within the first three years of their faculty careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial faculty appointments must have begun no earlier than May 31, 2022 and no later than May 31, 2025. Nominees must be able to serve as PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible disciplines / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplines that will be considered include physics, chemistry, mathematics, biology, astronomy, computer science, earth science, ocean science, and all branches of engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates engaged in research in the social sciences will not be considered. The program also directs support toward fields less generously funded than areas like clinical research, large national facility design/construction, and applied research directly relevant to national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional invitation and nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year, the Foundation invites the presidents of 50 universities to nominate two early-career professors each from their institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only presidents of the invited institutions (list provided) will receive requests for nominations; up to two nominations per invited president/institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination form content and restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed nomination form from the president of the university should state the nominee's name and contact information including email address, departmental affiliation, sponsoring institution's name, and president's name and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nomination form should not include any written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online nominee submission required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An online submission by each nominee should include: Complete contact information; departmental and institutional affiliation(s); disciplinary field(s); educational background; professional positions held; honors and awards; current external research support; publications; research statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominees cannot access the online application system until identified to the Packard Foundation. The online system will be available at fellows.packard.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research statement content and format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The research statement should describe why the research is important and outline the general goals for the next five years. The statement should also indicate, in general, how funds will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not need to be a detailed budget and will not be binding. The research statement is limited to 1,400 words (maximum two pages of text, prepared in 12-point font with 1-inch margins). If there are relevant figures, images or references, include these separately on a third page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation — quantity and required sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Four letters of recommendation are required: a recommendation from the nominee’s department head and recommendations from three people outside the nominee’s university who are personally familiar with the nominee's work and creative ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one external recommender must have had no supervisory or collaborative contact with the nominee. Department-head letters for joint appointments may be a single letter signed by both department heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation — content emphasis and length/format
rubrics_metrics.description: The department head letter should describe first-hand knowledge of the nominee's ability to do creative research and give emphasis to information not available in other letters of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should not exceed two pages and should be prepared in 12-point font with 1-inch margins. Letters may be uploaded in the online system or sent directly by email. Note: referees will not have access to the online system until the nominee enters their name and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis — creativity, risk-taking, and leadership potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program invests in future leaders who have the freedom to take risks, explore new frontiers in their fields of study, and follow uncharted paths that may lead to groundbreaking discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packard Fellows are described as inquisitive, passionate scientists and engineers who take a creative approach to their research, dare to think big, and follow new ideas wherever they lead. Selection favors highly creative early-career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference against well-established/well-funded applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship Program provides support for highly creative researchers early in their careers; faculty members who are well-established and well-funded are less likely to receive the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluation criterion: reviewers favor applicants who will benefit most from flexible early-career funding rather than those already well-funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on individual research and mentorship involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation emphasizes support for innovative individual research that involves the Fellows, their students, and junior colleagues, rather than extensions or components of large-scale, ongoing research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should foreground the nominee's individual role and the involvement of trainees/junior colleagues rather than positioning the proposal as a portion of a large, continuing program.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the program does not fund (areas with generous funding elsewhere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that certain areas of contemporary science and engineering already have access to relatively generous funding (for example, clinical research, research associated with the design and construction of large national facilities such as accelerators and space stations, and applied research of direct relevance to national security), the Packard Fellowships are directed to other, less generously supported fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in excluded or well-funded areas are less likely to be appropriate candidates for this fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: 20 recipients will receive individual grants of $875,000 distributed over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of the $175,000 paid each year, $17,500 is available to the university as compensation for administrative costs. The award is designed to allow maximum flexibility on how the funding is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements — annual narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must file annual narrative reports consisting of a brief, two-page description of research progress, a publication list, and updated curriculum vitae information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative report must be filed online (fellows.packard.org) by October 15 of each year. Reporting is kept to a minimum but is required because the award depends upon satisfactory research progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements — final financial report
rubrics_metrics.description: A final financial report must be submitted by December 31 of the final year of the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should outline actual expenditures for the entire grant period and should be submitted by the university’s financial office on behalf of the Fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship participation expectations (meetings and presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows within the first five years of their fellowship will be invited to participate in the annual Packard Fellows Meeting, held each fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to give an oral presentation on their work in their first and fifth years and are encouraged to make poster presentations in other years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and application timeline constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates for 2025: January 31 — Requests for nominations sent to university presidents; February 15 — online application system available; March 15 — nominations due to the Foundation; April 20 — all application materials must be submitted; October 15 — awards announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominees cannot access the online application system until the Foundation has been provided the nominee's identity by the university president. Applicants must meet these deadlines for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination Office Hours — advisory only
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will host 'Nomination Office Hours' for faculty members who might have specific questions about their eligibility for the 2025 Packard Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These meetings are optional and will not have any influence in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in award decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Packard Fellowships are awarded without regard to age, race, national origin, citizenship, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or physical disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit policy statement about equal opportunity in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, and inclusion pilot funding
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2021 the Foundation piloted a program to offer additional funding support to Fellows for activities that help increase diversity and representation in science and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pilot continued into 2022–2023, was reviewed in 2024, and the Foundation hopes to share invitation and details regarding continuation with the 2025 Fellows at the beginning of their grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative procedure — referee system access and submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees will not have access to the online system until the nominee enters their name and contact information into the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters may be submitted via file upload in the online system or sent directly to Foundation staff by email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program modification and Foundation discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: This program may be modified from time to time as experience is gained from its operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board of Trustees reserves the right to make any changes it considers desirable at any time; suggestions for modifications will be solicited from the Fellowship Advisory Panel and from Fellows.
